labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt is a PCR plate or PCR strips, and ELISA needs a flat plate or a deep-well plate
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is ELISA, which needs a flat plate or a deep-well plate as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 1, load name nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt), which is a PCR plate or PCR strips. A plate reader reads a flat, clear-bottomed plate, and an ELISA plate is coated before the samples arrive; a PCR plate is neither coated nor readable, and its thin-walled conical wells hold little and are meant for a thermocycler. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load a flat plate (corning_96_wellplate_360ul_flat or nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat) as the destination: it is what a plate reader reads and what an assay or a culture is done in.

check_text:
protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 error).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 0.78 ul, 1.56 ul, 3.12 ul, 6.25 ul and 1 more are below what the
p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 67:  p300.aspirate(std_vol, tuberack["A1"])
   At line 67 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.78 ul, 1.56 ul, 3.12 ul, 6.25 ul and 1
   more, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 10 times). A pipette cannot measure
   less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this
   protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [bc6ce33a7f02]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
